D-132 body capsule measured to intersect the desk collider (console_decision_0_col / _1_col / _2_col) at all three shipped use points, for both the 0.35x1.8 m and the 0.15x0.75 m capsule. Runtime use point == manifest authored use_m (delta 0.0000 m) at all three stations, so the causal chain manifest -> runtime use -> capsule failure is established by measurement, not inference.

findings.title: Option A's visible outcome is unmeasured while its gates are green, and A returns the pre-#379 foot-to-face distance that D-132/Mark rejected
findings.detail: The option table presents A as measured green on eight targets, but what Mark must approve is the visible result, and the doc marks renders UNMEASURED. The arithmetic is in the doc's own numbers plus mine: I measure the desk's collision face 0.15 m ahead of the feet at today's working points; A steps the feet 0.275 m back, so the face sits ~0.42 m ahead of the feet - essentially the pre-#379 relation the doc reports in V7 ('On 523d96f9 that face was 0.40 m away'), i.e. the configuration Mark rejected on 2026-10-29 ('The captain avatar appears misplaced and should be leaning on the console'). Option A restores D-132's clearance RULE unchanged but only partly restores its placement correction (advance 0.50 instead of 0.775). The doc states neither consequence, so Mark is asked to rule on a partially unmeasured, and in this respect one-sided, comparison.
findings.recommendation: Before the row resumes, state A's visible consequence explicitly (feet ~0.42 m from the desk face; how far the held pose's palms fall short of the console edge - to be measured in a render) and put it next to B's visible consequence, so the two options are compared on the axis Mark rules on.

findings.title: Read-only/unmapped record and provenance fields were never separated from the actionable visible contact behaviour
findings.detail: The record carries measured_7ae, first_collision_advance_m, walk_only_limits_m, measured_safe_limit_m, capsule, remaining and max_head_reach_m; the current test reads none of them (verified key by key), and asset-pins.json's layout_sha256 is read by no gate. These cannot turn a gate red or green. The actionable and visible items are the runtime working point, the body capsule against the desk collider, and the E/approach/panel sequence; and the console panel's buttons are screen-space (CanvasLayer) with the physical screens anchored by screen_ship_m, so a working-point change moves no button. The doc's D2 table maps read sources but does not classify read-only provenance against runtime-visible contact, and the round-1 report carried no such finding.
findings.recommendation: Add one line to D2 naming the read-only fields, so a future reader does not treat a recorded number as an enforced one.

findings.title: Option A's file set is still stated three ways (4 / 6 / 7); AC6 omits asset-pins.json
findings.detail: See the prior-findings table. The recommendation says seven files; the 'Estimated LOC' header lists four; AC6 lists manifest, bow_a and budgets only, so it names six files with S1. asset-pins.json's layout_sha256 re-pin is in neither list, although no gate reads it (verified), so it is provenance-only.
findings.recommendation: Make AC6 and the header list the same seven files before the executor runs.

findings.title: Risk row 'under 5 mm of slack' is not supported by the measurements
findings.detail: Option A advances 0.50 m from the original point; I measure the first D-132 capsule collision at 0.545-0.555 m of advance depending on the 5 mm grid anchor. The margin from A's point to the collision is therefore >=45 mm, not 'under 5 mm'. The doc's underlying bracket is right; the risk wording (and the 'measured_safe_limit_m' 0.525 vs advance 0.50 = 25 mm relation it is presumably describing) is what misleads.
findings.recommendation: Restate the risk with the measured numbers, or say plainly that the slack is 25 mm against the safe limit and ~50 mm against the first collision.

findings.title: first_collision_advance_m 0.55 sits at the optimistic edge of the measured bracket
findings.detail: Measured: 0.545 m of advance is clear, 0.550 m collides (exact-original anchor); with the doc's rounded table anchor the boundary is 0.555. The record's 0.55 is one grid step optimistic; it is a read-only field with no gate reading it, and option A's advance of 0.50 is unaffected.

findings.title: The visible-premise number 0.12 m is a bezel sub-part, not reproducible from the desk's collision box
findings.detail: I measure the nearest desk collision face 0.15 m ahead of the feet at h 0.70 and h 1.00 (and 0.26 m at h 1.05), inside a lateral sweep of +/-0.30 m whose minimum lands on the sweep edge, so the true minimum may be smaller. The doc's 0.12 m at h 0.70 and 0.13 m at h 1.00-1.05 is a bezel-surface figure (the visible frame), which the single desk collider does not expose. The two are not in conflict, but the doc's number is not reproducible from the collision geometry and I did not measure the bezel separately.
findings.recommendation: Say which geometry the 0.12 m refers to (visible bezel vs collider), so a future reader can reproduce it.
